- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days after a spike.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of downward trend in history + negative sentiment, model tends to ignore mean reversion; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply “early horizon discount” — reduce first 5 days by 1–2% relative to later days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.33), model tends to “smooth” extremes — adjust forecast to reflect volatility, especially if true outcome shows sharp reversals.
